articles.title: Alavés - Villarreal | Tratar de arrancar en Mendizorroza: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: El 'submarino' buscará su primera victoria en LaLiga. Buenas sensaciones de los vitorianos en el inicio. Pocos cambios en ambos onces. Mariano podría volver a ser suplente. Nathan Saliba está en la lista amarilla
articles.summary: El 'submarino' buscará su primera victoria en LaLiga. Buenas sensaciones de los vitorianos en el inicio. Pocos cambios en ambos onces. Mariano podría volver a ser suplente. Nathan Saliba está en la lista amarilla
articles.body: Tras comenzar el curso puntuando en las dos primeras jornadas, el Alavés afronta el primer desafío de magnitud. El Villarreal, que ha empatado los dos primeros partidos, aterriza en Mendizorroza para evaluar las buenas sensaciones vitorianas y para buscar su primer triunfo. Son todo noticias positivas, más allá del temor a que algún jugador importante pueda abandonar el barco en el cierre del mercado. Sin embargo, Quique sólo piensa en darle continuidad al buen juego. La mejoría defensiva es una evidencia, pero el Villarreal le exigirá estar a un gran nivel sin balón para poder dejar la puerta a cero. Sivera, que estrena renovación hasta 2030, tendrá más trabajo que en las dos anteriores semanas. Quique podría repetir el once del Rayo. Ville Koski, recuperado de las molestias que le obligaron a pedir el cambio en Butarque, apunta a ser de la partida. Y Mikel Rodríguez se mantendrá en la medular. Además, Mariano, que está siendo decisivo en este comienzo de temporada para el Alavés, podría empezar otra vez el encuentro desde el banquillo, pese a marcar en los dos primero partidos de LaLiga ante Getafe y Rayo Vallecano. Tras mejorar las sensaciones ante el Atlético, llega a Vitoria con la intención de estrenarse por fin en esta nueva era de Íñigo Pérez. El técnico no tiene bajas y cuenta con todo el plantel a sus disposición. La gran novedad es la entrada del canadiense Nathan Saliba, que llegó el pasado martes. Los amarillos apostarán por mantener la base del equipo de las dos primeras jornadas para buscar la victoria en un escenario que se les resiste en las últimas temporadas y en el que históricamente han sufrido para conseguir resultados. Blanco vs Pape Gueye. Lucha por el control del juego en la medular. Será una dura prueba para el jugador del conjunto vitoriano que se medirá a un equipo con uno de los centros del campo más poderosos del campeonato. El futbolista amarillo, además, ya ha firmado un tanto esta temporada. El Villarreal demostró fortaleza en el Metropolitano. El Alavés está bien, pero los amarillos, un equipo con muchos recursos, no pueden esperar mucho más para lograr su primera victoria.

articles.title: Have expensively-assembled Rangers improved at all under McInnes?
articles.summary: After crashing out of the Conference League, questions are mounting for Derek McInnes at Rangers, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
Where do you start? How do you catalogue the insipidness of Derek McInnes' Rangers team in Jablonec?

How do you catalogue the Pedro-Caixinha-in-the-bushes level embarrassment that the club experienced in their exit from European football on Thursday?

In Jablonec, Rangers were unspeakably awful, devoid of any cohesion, desire, threat, their manager reduced to saying how embarrassed and mortified he was multiple times post-match.

They had one shot on target the whole night, one goal scored in 210 minutes. Rangers fans in the stadium gave it to them with both barrels at the end.

McInnes apologised. The whole scene was cringe-making. He tried to explain what he was trying to do with his multiple switches of formation and attempted to explain why his side were "miles off it".

Talk is cheap in his position. There's a limited shelf life for that kind of thing at Ibrox.

The chat from some Rangers folk in the preamble was that the Conference League meant little to them, that an exit wouldn't spark an uprising, that no midweek European football could give them a chance to hurl themselves at the Premiership instead. Fine in theory, but not in reality.

The notion that a defeat would be met with a collective shrug by Rangers fans was never a serious proposition. This defeat sparked untrammelled fury.

McInnes would be as well staying away from social media. Winning in the bear pit of Pittodrie on Sunday is strongly advised.

Rangers out of Europe after wretched penalty defeat in Jablonec

'Mortified' McInnes takes responsibility for Rangers' European exit

Latest Rangers news, analysis and fan views

What are Rangers? What is their identity?

Rangers were so flat in the Czech Republic, meandering about like confused men, showing weakness in the tackle and not a scintilla of wit. McInnes changed the shape of his four or five times and the poverty of their play didn't improve one iota.

"I look at us now and I'm thinking, well, we're no' great as a possession-based team at the minute," said McInnes in explaining his constant switches.

"We're not a counter-attacking team enough, or effectively enough, at times. We don't look like a team who are happy when we go direct. And teams need to be something."

Quite. And what are Rangers? What's their identity? What are they good at? In what areas are they improving?

McInnes was appointed in June, had a full pre-season, had six games and then a week off to prepare for the trip to Jablonec, only for Rangers to produce their worst effort of this, and many other, seasons.

During the dog days of his reign at Rangers, Russell Martin was once asked if he could name one or two things that were better on his watch - and he couldn't do it.

If McInnes was asked the same question now then there's no guarantee that he would come up with an answer, or at least, an answer that rang true.

Nobody really knows what his Rangers are, least of all McInnes, you suspect. He made three substitutions at the break on Thursday, a trio that brought his total of half-time replacements to 11 in seven games.

That betrays a manager who has either got his team wrong in the first place, hasn't been able to impart his message to his starters or doesn't have a dressing room capable of taking in what he's saying to them. Whatever the truth of it, it's not good.

He knows what he wants because he watched it on television the night before. Hearts had four new players in their starting line-up against Rapid Vienna and used another two off the bench.

Wouter Vrancken, in quick time, moulded them together and made something terrific out of them in winning their own Conference League tie in Austria.

McInnes praised his old club for the resilience of their players and the stomach they showed for the fight. The inference being that his own boys had little or none of that. Again you ask, why not?

Vast periods of this play-off went by without Rangers stringing more than four and five passes together. They pressed in ones and two or not at all.

They came across as a team that had just met, a collection of guys rounded up in a pub and coached by a character who had no idea what to do with them.

Where was Raskin? And why not sign experience?

Ibrox is a confused place right now. McInnes said his team looked young and inexperienced against Jablonec. This was on the back of announcing the signing of a 20-year-old winger and - if things go to plan - a 22-year-old striker.

If they need gnarled operators then why not sign some?

There was no Nico Raskin, the midfielder left at home, not because there'd been a bid for him, said McInnes, but because there might be.

If there were was a decent offer and the possibility of higher ones, his absence would have been understandable. If there was no bid then why was there no Raskin?

He was missed, said McInnes. A player who performed well at the World Cup and he's left at home? Odd.

McInnes said that his coaching staff are "elite in everything we do" in preparing the players for games like this. That's a massive claim after losing the way they did.

The manager said that the responsibility for the failure was his but he repeatedly returned to how lamentable his players were. His players. Six of McInnes' signings started and another two came off the bench.

What has McInnes been doing with his expensively-assembled team. A dozen players have now been signed. How much money has to be spent before the manager starts to look convincing in the role?

The Rangers players who were on the field in the Czech Republic cost about £30m in transfer fees. The wage bill at Ibrox must be astronomical. They've now added the £8.5m winger Kim Min-su and may soon recruit a £9.5m striker in Kevin Kelsy.

The giant wad of cash splurged on all this would choke an elephant.

By contrast, Jablonec's record signing cost around £700,000. Their most recent turnover was £8.5m compared to Rangers' £94m. Their stadium is the size of a shoebox, their support tiny, their European story minimal.

They were the ones who went after the game, though. They didn't have a huge amount going for them in ability terms, but they had edge and character.

Hard work and energy? They trounced Rangers on all of the things that require no talent, just honesty.

McInnes is in a tight spot, not in any danger of losing his job, but with huge amounts of ground to make up with the fans.

He's been around a long time, but the pressure those supporters can exert when things are bad is a challenge for any manager, no matter how long he's been around.

Pittodrie next. A welcome, of sorts, awaits.

articles.title: Each Power Four conference adopts policy to ban pro football players from joining their respective conferences
articles.summary: The Big Ten made the first move on Tuesday, and the SEC followed suit. Next was the Big 12, and the ACC eventually went the same route.
articles.body:
Each of the Power Four conferences have banned pro football players from joining their respective leagues.

The ACC was the last of the group to adopt policy prohibiting that kind of comeback, which has gained sudden popularity as several members of the 2022 high school class eyeing a fifth year of eligibility have turned to the courts to challenge a new NCAA eligibility model that excludes them.

The Big Ten got the ball rolling on Tuesday , officially making football players ineligible if they signed pro contracts, appeared on an NFL roster or declared for the NFL Draft as underclassmen and didn't withdraw.

"The conference continues to evaluate potential rules restricting professional athletes in other sports from conference competition," the league said in a statement, in part.

The Big Ten later announced the penalties for violating the rule: a coach suspension of 50% of the season and an institutional fine .

Then on Tuesday afternoon, the SEC followed suit. The conference announced a similar policy but for both football and basketball.

Notre Dame officials have told the Big Ten and SEC that the school will also follow a policy of that ilk.

On Wednesday, the Big 12 passed a policy that bars athletes from competing in all sports.

The ACC's policy uses language akin to the SEC's, forbidding pro football and basketball defectors.

"The Board's action reflects the ACC's commitment to preserving college sports as an opportunity for college students that is clearly distinct from professional sports, protecting opportunities for current and future student-athletes and promoting competitive equity," the ACC said in a statement.

It wasn't just power conferences acting either, as the Mountain West announced the same policy hours after the ACC .

The flurry of discussions comes after the reports that former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright and former New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Zxavian Harris are leaving the pro ranks to play for LSU . Both Wright and Harris played for Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss.

Kiffin defended courting pro players on Monday during a press conference while being careful not to confirm any new signings, saying, "[They're] either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country."

On Monday, SEC presidents met virtually to support opposition to professional players coming back to play in college.

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference. Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition," read part of the SEC's statement.

With Tuesday's decision, SEC schools are no longer allowed to have such athletes on their rosters for football or basketball. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey was granted "full and unlimited authority," which includes suspending a school from competition, according to Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger .

With the power conferences all opting for guardrails to shield the integrity of college athletics, they could be subject to additional legal action. And, so, the leagues themselves may soon be at the center of new lawsuits — instead of the NCAA.

Dellenger highlighted that possibility in a post on X earlier this week:

"Important to note that league-wide rules do not absolve a conference from legal challenges," Dellenger wrote on Tuesday . "In fact, conferences will likely now be sued by athletes as defendants in separate lawsuits or added as defendants in existing lawsuits, many times in front of the same judges."

If conferences' hands are tied, and they can't even enforce the policies they've put forth, the conference commissioners and/or their presidents will have to figure out how they'd go about sanctioning schools directly for playing an athlete who's ineligible under these new parameters, per Dellenger .

articles.title: Double strike from Manisha powers Jharkhand to Subroto Cup U-17 girls' crown
articles.summary: Football News: NEW DELHI: Manisha produced the biggest performance of her young career as Jharkhand defeated NCC Aizawl 2-0 to lift the Junior Girls (U-17) title in .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Manisha produced the biggest performance of her young career as Jharkhand defeated NCC Aizawl 2-0 to lift the Junior Girls (U-17) title in the 65th Subroto Cup International Football Tournament at the Ambedkar Stadium on Thursday.The forward, wearing jersey No. 12, scored once in each half to settle a fiercely contested final and hand Jharkhand one of the most coveted trophies in Indian school football. Her clinical finishes in the 22nd and 43rd minutes proved enough to separate two evenly matched sides in front of an enthusiastic crowd.The victory capped a memorable campaign for Jharkhand, whose disciplined defending and quick transitions consistently troubled an NCC side that had impressed throughout the tournament. While NCC enjoyed spells of possession, Jharkhand remained composed under pressure and made the most of their chances in the final third.The breakthrough arrived midway through the opening half. After a sustained spell of attacking pressure, Manisha found space inside the box and calmly slotted home to give Jharkhand a deserved lead. The goal injected confidence into the side, with the midfield working tirelessly to deny NCC any rhythm before the interval.NCC responded positively after conceding and attempted to level the contest through attacks from the flanks, but Jharkhand goalkeeper Khushboo Kumari marshaled her defense superbly. Her assured handling and timely interceptions ensured the lead remained intact heading into the break.Jharkhand doubled their advantage just before halftime through the same source. Manisha once again timed her run to perfection and finished with conviction, leaving the goalkeeper with little chance. The second goal shifted the momentum firmly in Jharkhand's favor and gave the eventual champions a comfortable cushion.Despite trailing by two goals, NCC refused to surrender. The runners-up pressed aggressively after the restart and created a handful of promising opportunities, but Jharkhand's backline stood resolute. Khushboo continued to command her penalty area confidently, frustrating every attempt at a comeback as the clock ticked down.When the final whistle blew, jubilant celebrations erupted among the Jharkhand players and coaching staff, who embraced on the pitch after completing a remarkable title-winning run. The triumph also highlighted the growing strength of girls' football in the state, with the team displaying both technical quality and remarkable composure throughout the competition.The final formed the centerpiece of a colorful closing ceremony that celebrated the legacy of the Subroto Cup, now in its 65th edition. The day's festivities began with a spectacular aerial display by the Air Devil Sky Diving Team, followed by an impressive performance from the Air Warrior Drill Team. Students of the Air Force School added a cultural flourish with a vibrant dance presentation before kickoff.The title clash was attended by Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit PVSM AVSM VM VSM, Vice Chief of the Air Staff, who presented the trophies and medals as the chief guest. India women's national team footballer Jyoti Ann Burrett was the guest of honor and congratulated both finalists for showcasing the standard of emerging talent in Indian football.Individual excellence was also recognized during the prize distribution ceremony. Thuamdinpuii of NCC Aizawl was named the best player of the tournament and received a cash award of Rs 50,000 for her outstanding performances. Jharkhand's Khushboo Kumari took home the Best Goalkeeper award, while Beena Kerketta was adjudged the Best Coach after guiding her side to the championship. Mata Rukmanidevi High School of Chhattisgarh won the Best School award, and CISCE was honored with the Fair Play Award, with each recipient receiving Rs 50,000.For Jharkhand, however, the evening belonged to Manisha, whose match-winning brace ensured her team etched its name into Subroto Cup history with a commanding performance on the biggest stage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: De dominar el mercado a 'parados': la gran depreciación de las estrellas
articles.standfirst: Futbolistas que llegaron a valer una millonada y actualmente su precio se ha hundido y se encuentran sin equipo
articles.summary: Futbolistas que llegaron a costar una millonada y actualmente
articles.body: Un día fueron los futbolistas más cotizados y valorados del mercado. Un gran número de clubes se peleaban por ellos, eran los más deseados del panorama, y actualmente, se encuentran sin equipo, buscando una nueva oportunidad para intentar llegar a ser lo que se esperaba de ellos. Jóvenes promesas sobre los que se pusieron grandes expectativas, pero que no lograron llegar a cumplirlas. El extremo inglés es uno de los que encabeza esta lista. Canterano del Watford y del Manchester City, emigró a Alemania para demostrar su talento en busca de una oportunidad con el primer equipo. Fue en el Borussia Dortmund donde explotó. "Estamos encantados de que Jadon Sancho, actualmente una de las mayores promesas del fútbol europeo, quiera jugar en el Borussia Dortmund y vaya a hacerlo. Estamos convencidos de que podremos ayudar a este joven jugador a seguir desarrollando su juego y a convertirlo en una valiosa incorporación a nuestro equipo a medio plazo", declaró el director deportivo del club alemán Michael Zorc en la presentación de Sancho. A base de números comenzó a colarse entre los mejores del mundo en su posición. La 19/20 fue su mejor año en el país germano, 20 goles y 20 asistencias en 44 partidos. Precisamente, cuando alcanzó el mayor valor de mercado de su carrera, 130 millones de euros. Regresó a Manchester, pero para jugar con el United, a cambio de 85 millones de euros. Quiso volver a su país, y probar en la Premier League, pero si en Alemania había vivido un sueño, en Inglaterra fue una pesadilla. Apenas cinco goles en su primera campaña con los 'Red Devils'. Con el paso del tiempo, la situación no fue a mejor, en su tercer año, fue apartado por Ten Hag, con el que no tuvo una gran relación. Por ello, decidió buscar una vía de escape, regresando donde mostró su mejor versión, el Borussia Dortmund en enero de 2024. Las sensaciones fueron buenas, con un buen nivel del inglés que recordaba en cierta medida a ese joven que enamoró al Signal Iduna Park unos años atrás y ayudó a su equipo a llegar a la final de la Champions League, aunque cayeron contra el Real Madrid. "Conocemos su calidad y hoy la hemos vuelto a comprobar. Quizás no sea tan fácil trasladarlo al campo, especialmente cuando no has tenido ritmo durante un tiempo", afirmó Edin Terzic, el técnico del conjunto alemán en ese momento. Sin embargo, su sueño en vida solo duró hasta final de temporada. Tuvo que volver a Mánchester, aunque solo defendió la camiseta del United siete minutos más, ya que encadenó cesiones a Chelsea y Aston Villa, con los que ganó la Conference y la Europa League respectivamente. A pesar de ello, ninguno de los dos clubes decidió hacerse con sus servicios. Este verano, el Manchester United no ha renovado su contrato, por lo que a sus 26 años y con 18 millones de valor de mercado, está buscando equipo donde resurgir. Otro futbolista que comenzó a despuntar desde muy joven es Raheem Sterling. El también extremo inglés se incorporó a la academia del Liverpool en 2010, y desde ahí comenzaría su carrera profesional. En la 12/13 comenzó a ser parte fundamental del primer equipo y con solo 17 años anotó su primer gol en la Premier League. "Es un verdadero talento que hay que cultivar", comentaba Brendan Rodgers sobre él. Tal era su proyección y nivel dentro del campo, que en 2014 recibió el Golden Boy, seleccionándole como el mejor joven del mundo. Ese estatus le llevó a cambiar de equipo un año después, siendo una de las principales piezas del Manchester City para su nuevo proyecto, a cambio de 63 millones de euros. La llegada de Guardiola al club inglés fue clave para el extremo, sacando su mejor versión. En 2019 fue cuando alcanzó su mayor valor, tasado en 160 millones de euros. "Es un jugador extraordinario. Todo el mérito de su mejora es suyo. Lo ha hecho él. Además tiene un físico increíble, se recupera muy rápido, podría jugar otro partido mañana mismo. Depende de él saber lo bueno que puede llegar a ser", afirmó el técnico español sobre él en 2019. Sin embargo, tres años después, se marchó del Manchester City en un movimiento del que no levantaría cabeza. Después de siete años, 131 goles y 11 títulos, continuó su carrera en el Chelsea tras ser traspasado por 56 millones de euros. Su producción goleadora se redujo en cierta medida, sumado a que el conjunto londinense no pasó por un buen rendimiento colectivo los dos siguientes años. El primero no se clasificó a competiciones europeas y el segundo fueron a Conference. Maresca llegó al banquillo 'blue' y no contaba con el inglés, por lo que tuvo que buscar una salida cedido en otro club de la ciudad, el Arsenal. "Han cambiado muchas cosas desde que estuvimos juntos. Pero veo que tiene hambre. Tiene mucha energía y ganas de demostrar. Nos hará mejores", comentó Arteta sobre su decisión de traerlo. Sin embargo, Sterling estaba muy lejos de su mejor forma. Tan solo pudo aportar a los 'gunner' un único tanto en toda la temporada. Regresó al Chelsea, pero fue apartado por el club, sin disputar ni un solo minuto en la primera parte de la temporada. En enero de este año, el club de Londres comunicó que separaban sus caminos de "mutuo acuerdo". Tras unos días sin contrato, firmó por el Feyenoord, para intentar levantar su carrera, pero tras ocho partidos en los que solo dio una asistencia, el club neerlandés no le ha renovado. Unos años después de tocar la cima, Raheem Sterling se encuentra sin equipo a sus 31 años y con un valor de mercado de tres millones de euros. Otra joven promesa de la Premier League fue Dele Alli. Se formó en el MK Dons y el Tottenham le fichó en febrero de 2015 tras una gran primera mitad de temporada, aunque se incorporó a las filas de los 'Spurs' en verano. Rápidamente se hizo con un puesto de titular en la plantilla, y en su primer año llegó a las dobles cifras en goles y asistencias. "No hay nada más que decir. Habla en el campo. Es joven y tiene un gran potencial para mejorar. ¿Qué más puedo decir? Está demostrando un gran talento", afirmó Mauricio Pochettino en enero de 2017. Su mejor versión se vio esa temporada, la 17/18, en la que aportó 22 goles y 13 asistencias para el Tottenham, ganando por segundo año consecutivo el premio a mejor futbolista joven de la Premier League y llegando a estar valorado en 100 millones de euros. El siguiente año firmó unos números similares, pero con el paso del tiempo, su relevancia fue a menos, en gran parte por las lesiones. La irregularidad comenzó a pasarle factura, algo de lo que Mourinho, su nuevo entrenador en los 'Spurs', le advirtió cuando dirigía al club inglés. "Hay una gran diferencia de un jugador que mantiene la consistencia y un jugador que tiene momentos y eso es lo que marca la diferencia entre un jugador top y un jugador con un gran potencial. Deberías exigirte más de ti mismo, no yo. Ni nadie. Tú. Te tienes que pedir más a ti mismo", afirmó el portugués. Dele Alli comenzó a pasar por una mala etapa no solo futbolística, también mental. "A los 24, hacer lo que amo, para mí fue desgarrador", afirmó en una entrevista con Gary Neville, en la que desveló todas las dificultades de su infancia, como sufrir abusos sexuales a los seis años, traficar con drogas a los ocho o atravesar problemas con el alcohol. Su importancia en el equipo comenzó a caer, y se marchó al Everton en enero de 2022 para intentar retomar el vuelo. No tuvo una gran participación con los 'Toffees', salvándose del descenso en la última jornada, y ese mismo verano salió cedido al Besiktas. Sin embargo, su nuevo capítulo tampoco fue bien. "Creo que en este estado no merece jugar en el once. Su situación actual no cumplió con nuestras expectativas en términos de integridad del equipo", declaró el entrenador del club turco Şenol Güneş. Además, un desgarro muscular provocó que su 'erasmus' en Turquía acabase antes. Regresó al Everton, pero sus problemas físicos y mentales no le permitieron volver a vestir la camiseta. En verano de 2024 se quedó sin club, y no fue hasta enero del siguiente año, cuando volvió a tener equipo. Cesc Fábregas lo incorporó a su Como, pero de nuevo, tuvo un paso para olvidar. Tan solo representó los colores durante nueve minutos, que le sirvieron para recibir una tarjeta roja. Tras este capítulo en Italia, Dele Alli se volvió a quedar sin trabajo en verano de 2025 y desde entonces, no ha vuelto a vestirse de corto. A sus 30 años y con un millón de euros de valor, es uno de los futbolistas que figuran como agente libre. Una de las tantas perlas francesas que han surgido en los últimos años. Canterano del Olympique de Lyon, que llegó a debutar con el primer equipo con tan solo 17 años. Sin embargo, tuvo que marcharse al Mónaco, que pagó cinco millones por su traspaso antes de cumplir la mayoría de edad. Fue allí donde explotó en su segunda temporada, la 14/15. 12 goles y cuatro asistencias firmó ese año. Su rendimiento le llevó a recibir el Golden Boy y ser convocado por primera vez con las selección absoluta francesa. "Tiene potencia y velocidad. Es joven, pero su perfil me interesa para una posición donde no es fácil encontrar esas cualidades. Tiene un potencial interesante", comentaba Deschamps sobre el joven delantero. El Manchester United, en unos años sin ganar títulos y de reconstrucción, necesitaban talentos generacionales. Y Martial parecía serlo. Por ello, decidieron arriesgar y ficharle por 60 millones de euros en el último día de mercado del verano de 2015. Y en su primer día, respondió a las expectativas. Gol en 30 minutos para certificar la victoria contra el Liverpool. Su primer año, terminó como máximo goleador del equipo con 17 tantos, y ayudó al United a volver a conquistar un título, la FA Cup. Pero tras llegar Mourinho al club, hizo que Martial perdiese protagonismo, y con ello, frenase su proyección. Sin embargo, con la llegada de Solskjaer al banquillo 'red', el francés mostró su mejor versión, 23 goles y 12 asistencias en 48 partidos. "Anthony es un jugador vital para nosotros" o "Si quiere estar al nivel de Cristiano, Anthony sabe lo que tiene que hacer. Depende de él. Tiene el talento", eran algunas de las afirmaciones del técnico noruego sobre Martial. Aunque ese gran año, fue un espejismo. El año siguiente, sus cifras bajaron hasta marcar tan solo siete goles y repartir nueve asistencias. Una decadencia que fue aumentando con el paso de los años. Tras jugar apenas 11 partidos con Rangnick en los primeros seis meses de la 21/22, puso rumbo al Sevilla cedido para levantar su carrera, aunque terminó teniendo un paso muy discreto. Regresó al Manchester, y no pudo recuperar su nivel. En septiembre de 2024 llegó libre al AEK Atenas y un año después el Monterrey pagó un millón por su fichaje. Su etapa en México no fue buena, llegó a estar apartado por una supuesta indisciplina y abandonó el club este verano. Con 30 años y un valor de mercado de 3,5 millones de euros, Martial sigue buscando colores que vestir. Tras destacar en las categorías inferiores del Vasco da Gama, un joven Philippe Coutinho emigró rápido para explotar su talento, firmando a los 16 años con el Inter a cambo de 3,8 millones de euros, aunque llegó a Italia a los 18. Rafa Benítez le dio importancia en su primera temporada como 'nerazurri', aunque una lesión de rodilla le hizo perderse una gran cantidad de partidos. Pochettino pidió su cesión para el Espanyol en la segunda mitad de la 11/12. Tras volver de la cesión y no tener los minutos esperados en Milán, el brasileño salió al Liverpool a cambio de 13 millones de euros en enero de 2013. "Creo que Coutinho tiene la misma calidad que Ronaldinho y Messi", afirmó el entrenador argentino tras la llegada de Coutinho a Inglaterra. Desde su llegada fue un jugador muy importante en el esquema inglés, donde se convirtió en leyenda. Año tras año, Coutinho iba mejorando como futbolista y siendo más importante para el Liverpool. En la 16/17 alcanzó su mejor año en cifras con el conjunto 'red', 14 goles y nueve asistencias en 31 partidos. Además de ser uno de los grandes talentos del panorama, fue uno de los emblemas de la reconstrucción por la que pasó el Liverpool, pero se marchó sin ganar ningún título. El brasileño quería la Champions, y aprovechó una oportunidad única. En enero de 2018, el Barcelona pagó 135 millones de euros, diez veces más de lo que invirtió la entidad inglesa años atrás, para que Coutinho se uniese a Messi y Suárez para volver a conquistar Europa. Aunque tuvo que ver como su exequipo le eliminaba y la levantaba una temporada después. Tras un año y medio como culé, no terminó de convencer, y se le buscó una salida al Bayern para volver a encontrar su mejor forma. Pero en Alemania tampoco encontraría su lugar. Comenzó siendo muy importante con Niko Kovac, pero tras su destitución y el nombramiento de Flick como nuevo técnico, perdió protagonismo. Cabe destacar en su paso por Múnich, los dos goles y la asistencia en la goleada 2-8 al Barça, el equipo al que pertenecía. Regresó a España, pero una rotura de menisco provocó que se perdiese una gran cantidad de partidos y su nivel decayese. En enero de 2022 salió cedido al Aston Villa, club que decidió comprarle confiando en que recuperase su nivel. Sin embargo, la sustitución de Emery por Gerrard en el banquillo fue la peor noticia para Coutinho. El español dejó de contar con él, y el brasileño tuvo que marcharse. Encadenó cesiones a Al-Duhail SC y Vasco da Gama, al que se marchó libre en 2025. Cuando parecía que en su regreso al club del que salió sería una gran etapa, en febrero de este mismo año decidió acabar el contrato que estaban en vías de renovar por su "salud mental". Después de llegar a ser el segundo fichaje más caro de la historia del fútbol, a sus 34 años se encuentra sin equipo y con un valor de mercado de 2,5 millones de euros.

articles.title: Vuelve la BundesBayern
articles.standfirst: Kompany busca su tercera Liga de forma consecutiva • Cambios en el Dortmund y Leipzig • Expectación con Carles Martínez en el Leverkusen
articles.summary: Kompany busca su tercera Liga de forma consecutiva • Cambios en el Dortmund y Leipzig • Expectación con Carles Martínez en el Leverkusen
articles.body: El histórico título conquistado por Xabi Alonso y su Bayer Leverkusen, único campeón invicto en la historia del fútbol alemán, fue un oasis en mitad del desierto. De la mano de Vincent Kompany, la ‘BundesBayern’ vuelve a ser una realidad. Sumado al título de POKAL seis años después y las semifinales alcanzadas en Champions, el Bayern revalidó el título de Bundesliga con una suficiencia aplastante: arrancó con nueve victorias, se mantuvo invicto toda la primera vuelta, sólo cedió una derrota en toda la temporada... y superó al Real Madrid 11-12 como el equipo más goleador (122) de las grandes ligas en el Siglo XXI. Kompany no tiene ninguna intención de bajarse del trono y arranca su tercera campaña en el Allianz Arena con la misión de igualar los tres títulos de Liga consecutivos que lograron Udo Lattek (1972-1974 y 1985-1987), Ottmar Hitzfeld (1999-2001) y su mentor Guardiola (2014-2016). Para ello, no sólo han mantenido intacta la estructura que han ido solidificando durante estas dos temporadas, sino que le han añadido elementos nuevos para seguir elevando el nivel. Más allá de quedarse en propiedad con Bara Sapoko Ndiaye y recuperar a Arijon Ibrahimovic, han invertido 100 millones para que ‘Nene’ Brown solucione las carencias en el lateral izquierdo a raíz de los continuos problemas acarreados por Davies y para que Saibari sume más ‘dinamita’ si cabe al demoledor ataque que forman Olise, Kane y Luis Díaz. Esperan recuperar la mejor versión de Musiala y, como fondo de armario, están Gnabry y el joven Lennart Karl. El Bayern, salvo sorpresa, no va a dar opción. Pero, por lo que pueda llegar a pasar, Borussia Dortmund y Leipzig deben intentar encontrar la mayor regularidad posible para estirar la lucha por el título lo máximo posible y, al menos, intentar evitar que los de Kompany vuelvan a ser el campeón más madrugador de la grandes ligas. El Dortmund es quien más dispuesto parece a alterar esta realidad. En marzo se nombró como nuevo director deportivo a un Ole Book que ha recuperado la apuesta por el talento joven; Gadou, Karetsas, Konstantelias... La única incorporación que supera los 23 años es Veerman. El Leipzig, por su parte, prescindió de los servicios de Ole Werner, a pesar de lograr la clasificación a Champions, para nombrar a Martín Demichelis como nuevo entrenador. Se han movido poco, eso sí, a pesar de tener dinero en caja tras convertir a Diomande en la venta más cara de su historia. A ese vagón tratará de subirse el nuevo Leverkusen de Carles Martínez Novell. El mercado, desde luego, ilusiona. El plan pasa por volver a Champions, donde parece haberse instalado Hoeness con el Stuttgart. Por detrás, el Hoffenheim tratará de mantener el pulso por Europa con Friburgo, Eintracht... pero no un Wolfsburgo que ha descendido por primera vez. En compensación, vuelve un histórico como el Schalke. Corría el verano de 2012 cuando Dani Carvajal, en calidad de cedido desde el Real Madrid, abrió la vía española en las filas del Bayer Leverkusen para que, sólo un año después, Andrés Palop disfrutase de su última temporada como profesional. Fue Fernando Carro, CEO del club desde 2018, quien volvió a transitar por este sendero para convertir al equipo de la aspirina en nuestra gran colonia dentro de la Bundesliga. Hoy por hoy, cuenta con cuatro de los siete representantes españoles que tenemos en el campeonato alemán. Tras una temporada ‘post’ Xabi Alonso lejos del nivel esperado que les obligó a pegar varios ‘volantazos’, el acento español vuelve al banquillo del BayArena con el nombramiento de Carles Martínez Novell como nuevo entrenador tras tres temporadas magníficas en Francia a los mandos de un Toulouse con el que alcanzó las semifinales de Coupe el curso pasado. No llega sólo a este Bayer Leverkusen, puesto que Miguel Gutiérrez ha hecho las maletas después de un sólo año en Nápoles para recoger el testigo que dejó en banda izquierda una leyenda del club como Xabi Alonso. Lucas Vázquez y Aleix García le han acogido con los brazos abiertos. Chema Andrés, al igual que Miguel Gutiérrez, también se formó en la cantera del Real Madrid y, tras un primer año de adaptación bastante positivo en el que llegó a disputar 39 partidos, arranca su segunda campaña en un Stuttgart de Champions y finalista de POKAL con el objetivo de afianzarse en el doble pivote junto a Stiller. Desde el Valladolid, sin coste de traspaso alguno, llega Chuki al Werder Bremen para convertirse en el segundo jugador español en la historia del club tras Alejandro Gálvez, quien vistió la camiseta entre 2014 y 2016. El último en saltar del barco ha sido Bryan Zaragoza. Tras un año cedido en el Celta primero y la Roma después, el Bayern lo ha vuelto a mandar a préstamo al Espanyol hasta final de temporada.

articles.title: Mbappé tiene rivales: Raphinha y Fermín amenazan su reinado en el Pichichi
articles.standfirst: Los tres suman tres goles
articles.summary: Los tres suman tres goles
articles.body: Raphinha y Fermín han arrancado la temporada 26-27 en un estado de forma excepcional. Hansi Flick está colocando al brasileño de falso 9, ante la salida de Robert Lewandowski y de Ferran Torres y la ausencia de un fichaje en punta, y el internacional está exhibiendo su potencial goleador. Pero el andaluz, desde la mediapunta, también está resaltando. Ambos suman tres tantos y amenazan el reinado de Mbappé en el Pichichi. El francés también ha festejado tres dianas en estos dos primeros encuentros. Flick y el Barça lo tienen claro. Quieren reforzar su ataque con Julián Álvarez, pero si el internacional argentino del Atlético de Madrid no firma por el Barça, no llegará ningún otro futbolista. Entre otros motivos porque el técnico y Deco consideran que hay opciones más que solventes en el vestuario. La principal, Raphinha, como el brasileño está demostrando. Pero no es el único. El Barça va sobrado de gol. El exfutbolista del Leeds firmó un doblete contra el Elche y rubricó otro tanto contra el Athletic. El internacional, que el curso pasado marcó 13 goles en LaLiga y 21 entre todas las competiciones, ya suma tres dianas en los dos primeros partidos. Su arranque está siendo sobresaliente. Flick le mantuvo sobre el terreno de juego contra el conjunto vasco hasta el minuto 62, cuando dio entrada a Dani Olmo, otra de sus opciones para la punta del ataque. Pero Fermín, desde la mediapunta, también está exhibiendo su puntería. Como el brasileño, el canterano firmó un doblete contra el Elche y también vio puerta contra el Athletic. El Barça suma siete goles en este inicio, y tres son del centrocampista y otros tres, de Raphinha. El otro lo firmó Adeyemi en el Martínez Valero. Los dos futbolistas azulgranas amenazan el reinado de Kylian Mbappé. El francés ganó el trofeo en las dos últimas temporadas (en la 24-25 festejó 31 tantos y en la 25-26, 25) y este curso también se estrenó con acierto: marcó tres goles esta jornada en el cruce del Real Madrid contra la Real Sociedad. LaLiga no ha hecho nada más que comenzar, pero la disputa ya promete.

articles.title: El Inter Miami ficha al argentino 'Kily' González para relevar a Hoyos en el banquillo
articles.standfirst: El club busca un revulsivo por la mala racha de resultados
articles.summary: El club busca un revulsivo por la mala racha de resultados
articles.body: El Inter Miami anunció este jueves el fichaje del argentino Cristian Alberto 'Kily' González como su nuevo entrenador, en sustitución de su compatriota Guillermo Hoyos, quien dejará el cargo sumido en una crisis de resultados. González se encontraba sin equipo desde que dejó el Platense en octubre de 2025. El exjugador del Real Zaragoza, Valencia o Inter Milán, entre otros equipos, asumirá las riendas "una vez que reciba los permisos de trabajo correspondientes", explicó en un comunicado el Inter Miami. Hasta entonces, Hoyos continuará sentándose en el banquillo, agregó el club, sin aclarar cuál será el futuro del actual técnico. Hoyos asumió el cargo el pasado abril después de que Javier Mascherano, el entrenador con el que el Inter Miami conquistó la última MLS Cup, renunciase alegando motivos personales. Hoyos, director deportivo del club antes de la marcha de Mascherano, comenzó con una buena racha de triunfos, pero los resultados empeoraron en el último mes, en el que cayó eliminado de la Leagues Cup y no conoce la victoria en la Major League Soccer (MLS). El argentino no podrá despedirse de su público este sábado ante el Montreal, puesto que la MLS le sancionó con un partido por incumplir reiteradamente la política de inicio tardío de partidos de la liga. El Inter Miami ocupa la segunda plaza en la Conferencia Este con 39 puntos, a 10 de distancia del Nashville, que le vapuleó por 4-1 hace dos semanas.

articles.title: FPL gameweek two tips: Bruno Fernandes or Erling Haaland for captain? Sell Man Utd assets?
articles.summary: BBC Sport FPL expert Pras looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing FPL managers heading into gameweek two, including whether to captain Erling Haaland or Bruno Fernandes.
articles.body:
We are only one week into the Fantasy Premier League season and already there have been some surprise results, with Manchester United and Liverpool disappointing in particular.

BBC Sport FPL expert Pras looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing FPL managers heading into gameweek two.

Pras' big advice this week is that the "smartest play right now is patience".

"One blank does not make a player finished, and one haul does not make him essential," he said. "Every gameweek adds information. Use it, do not chase it."

Is it too early to jump off Manchester United assets?

The 2-0 loss at Hull was unexpected, and plenty of managers are sitting on two or three United players. That does not mean you have to move this week.

Ipswich at home is still a good fixture and a good chance for Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo to respond.

If they blank again, the exits are clean: Bruno (£12m) into Cole Palmer (£9.5m) or Antoine Semenyo (£8.5m); Mbeumo (£8m) into Morgan Rogers (£7.5m) or Phil Foden (£7m).

However, I would give them this game against Ipswich first before making any decision.

Brentford midfielder Mamadou Sangare looks a very good prospect. He can rack up defensive contribution points (defcon) and he is already getting involved in the attack - as seen by his two assists against Spurs.

His price has gone up to £5.6m already, but that does not mean you have to buy him now.

He is still a defensive midfielder and those players tend to trickle points rather than explode every week. There is a slight overreaction in the community after one strong debut.

Find a window later - for example when you play a wildcard - to buy him. You do not have to force him in this gameweek.

How many Chelsea players should you bring in?

Joao Pedro is so widely owned that if you want extra bite from Chelsea 's attack, you almost have to look at Palmer or Rogers.

Both are good options, but the right entry point is gameweek four.

Palmer had a slight niggle late against Fulham , and Chelsea face Arsenal in gameweek three. Unless there is a major injury elsewhere in your team, hold off this week.

Eventually, owning two or three from Joao Pedro, Palmer and Rogers is a viable tactic.

Newcastle away was a difficult place to start for Alexander Isak (£9m), especially against his old club. The real test is this week at home to Nottingham Forest . Give him that game.

Liverpool are likely to make attacking additions, such as Bradley Barcola from Paris St-Germain , that should help him, and the fixtures after this look useful, with Ipswich and Fulham in gameweeks three and four.

One awkward away day is not enough evidence to sell.

Stay patient. Watch the next set of fixtures. Let the picture settle before you spend transfers you may need later.

Who should you captain: Haaland or Fernandes?

The biggest dilemma this week is who to back for captaincy.

Manchester City 's Erling Haaland is away at Crystal Palace . Bruno Fernandes is at home to Ipswich.

Despite the gameweek one disappointment, I would still back Fernandes.

The fixture is easier, and Manchester United need a reaction.

Without Jeremy Doku, City have not looked as sharp either, so I am inclined to give it to the midfielder who gets more points for a goal, clean sheet and defcon possibilities etc.

The multiple route to points make Fernandes a better captain in my view.

articles.title: Crystal Palace vs Manchester City – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park on Friday in a crucial Premier League clash as both sides look to secure three vital points.Pierre Sage...
articles.body:
Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park on Friday in a crucial Premier League clash as both sides look to secure three vital points.

Pierre Sage lost his first game in charge at Everton while Enzo Maresca needed a stoppage-time turnaround to beat Bournemouth in his own opener. City's recent dominance of this fixture is considerable — just two defeats in their last 22 league meetings with Palace, and no away loss to these opponents in the top flight since April 2015 — but Sage's side produced enough at Goodison Park to suggest sharper finishing could yield a different outcome here.

The game also carries a personal subplot. Marc Guehi returns to Selhurst Park for the first time since his January move from Palace to City, where he has already made an impact, scoring the equaliser that turned last weekend's win over Bournemouth. New City signing Ayyoub Bouaddi, an £86 million arrival from Lille, completed this week, could also be involved for the first time since finalising his transfer.

Crystal Palace vs Manchester City – Match preview and team news

Date: Friday, 28 August 2026 Kick-off: 20:00 BST Venue: Selhurst Park Referee: Andy Madley VAR: Stuart Attwell Last meeting: Manchester City 3-0 Crystal Palace, Premier League, 13 May 2026

Ismaila Sarr continues individual training and will again be absent with a groin injury. Chadi Riad remains sidelined after being stretchered off against Everton, with the club fearing a longer-term knee problem. Jean-Philippe Mateta started that game and, despite ongoing uncertainty over his contract, Sage has maintained that the striker's focus remains on his football and expects him to lead the line again.

Jeremy Doku is unavailable with a calf injury, and Matheus Nunes remains short of full fitness as he continues his recovery. Elliot Anderson, substituted against Bournemouth, has been confirmed fit by Maresca, who attributed the change to cramp rather than injury. Marc Guehi, used in an unfamiliar midfield role against Bournemouth, is expected to retain that position on his return to south London.

Sage's opening game brought defeat, but Palace's underlying numbers — 1.96 expected goals to Everton's 1.12 — suggested a more clinical side could have taken something from Goodison Park. The summer has been complicated by unresolved situations involving Mateta and Sarr, both linked with moves away, which Sage has worked to keep separate from matchday matters. A first home fixture of the season offers a chance to settle into the role in front of his own supporters.

Maresca's tenure began with a heavy Community Shield defeat to Arsenal before a much-needed response against Bournemouth, City recovering from a goal down through late goals from Guehi and Josko Gvardiol. The new manager is yet to oversee a clean sheet, and City won only two of their final five away league fixtures last season — a pattern he will want to address quickly on the road.

Manchester City predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Lewis, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol; Kovacic, Guehi; Foden, O'Reilly, Semenyo; Haaland

articles.body:
Manchester City travel to Selhurst Park on Friday looking to build on a hard-fought opening-weekend win, Enzo Maresca's side having come from behind to beat Bournemouth in his first Premier League match in charge.

The trip also returns Marc Guehi to the club he left for City in January, seven months on from that move.

Jeremy Doku remains out with a calf injury, and Matheus Nunes is not yet considered fully fit as he continues his recovery. Elliot Anderson, withdrawn against Bournemouth, has been confirmed fit by Maresca, who attributed the substitution to cramp rather than injury.

New signing Ayyoub Bouaddi, a £86 million arrival from Lille, completed this week, has been declared fit and available. "He is ready; he was working with his former club, so he is fit," Maresca said. "We will see how long it is in terms of adaptation, but for sure, he is ready to go."

Maresca is expected to persist with Guehi in a midfield role after his impact from that position against Bournemouth, where he also scored the equaliser. "We will see. It is an option," the head coach said when asked whether the arrangement would continue.

Rico Lewis could keep his place at right-back despite criticism of City's defensive display last weekend, though Abdukodir Khusanov remains an alternative option out wide. Phil Foden, Nico O'Reilly and Antoine Semenyo are set to support Erling Haaland in attack, with Bouaddi more likely to be introduced from the bench given his age and the club's stated intention to manage his workload carefully.

articles.title: Electronic Arts signs the Bundesliga to a multi-year deal worth €250 million
articles.summary: FC Bayern will be among a host of clubs featured in one of the most popular football games
articles.body:
According to a report by Sport Bild (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia), the Bundesliga signed a seven-year contract with Electronic Arts or EA for the licensing rights to the teams and players of the league:

This means the game will feature accurate images of the club, its players, the logos, and everything else in between; in the case of this deal, all 36 teams in Germany's top two leagues will feature on the game.

If a club isn't licensed on the game, then it uses a default club name and logo that alludes to the real-life team that it's based on. Historically speaking, the affected teams are mostly Italian clubs: Piemonte Calcio (Juventus), Milano FC (AC Milan), Lombardia FC (Inter Milan), Napoli FC (Napoli), and Bergamo Calcio (Atalanta).

As an avid FC Mobile (previously called FIFA Mobile) player, this is a big thing because it means I can keep on using Bayern players in my team. I've played the game continuously (for the most part) since its release in 2016, and the experience has taught me the ins and outs of the game, meta players and tactics, and a lot of the nitty gritty stuff.

Enough with the shameless plugging, this is a good deal for Bayern and the other 35 clubs in the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga even if the game severely underrates the Bavarians.

articles.title: Dragons' Den offers Peterborough street artist advice - and a job
articles.summary: Nathan Murdoch is offered a job painting one of the Dragon's offices in London.
articles.body:
A street artist who appeared on the BBC Dragons' Den came away with an offer of both professional advice - and a job.

Nathan Murdoch, 38, runs Street Arts Hire and has painted several murals in Peterborough, including tributes to Prodigy singer Keith Flint, and a Jude Bellingham portrait during the football World Cup.

He said he went on the show looking for further investment in his arts business, but all the Dragons agreed instead that he needed sound advice in order to expand.

Entrepreneur Steven Bartlett was so taken with Murdoch's work he offered the artist both one-to-one advice and a job painting the walls of his new London offices.

Murdoch appeared before the entrepreneurs accompanied by a large painting of a dragon - which he had created for the show.

He was asking for a £60,000 investment in return for a 10% share in his company.

The money, he said, would help employ a full-time role co-ordinating the work he and other artists were commissioned to do, as he said they could only currently fill about 60% of requests.

Murdoch is well known in Peterborough and in February he hosted an exhibition, Diesel Streets, celebrating more than two decades of graffiti and the city's street art culture.

The quality of his art stunned all five Dragons on the show, which aired on 27 August on BBC One.

Looking at the dragon painting brought in by Murdoch, Bartlett said: "You make me feel like a muggle just looking at that, thinking that a human being could do that versus what I can do. It's incredible."

Gary Neville said: "The artwork is absolutely stunning. You're taking home only £30,000 a year but you're a creative, you're a genius."

Pointing at the painting, which took Murdoch four hours to create, he said: "That's worth thousands of pounds", and quipped he would pay £5,000 for it.

Bartlett asked how much Murdoch charged a day, to which he replied: "About £600."

While none of them agreed to invest £60,000, all agreed he needed advice to help grow the business and suggested he could make far more money than he currently did.

Bartlett said he would give an hour of his time to sit with Murdoch and draw up a business plan.

He added: "I will pay you five times your day rate to do our new London HQ which has completely blank walls."

Murdoch had entered the den saying: "What have I got to lose?"

Leaving it with expert advice and a job offer, he said: "Although I didn't get the investment today, the advice I got was kind of what I needed to hear and overall it's been a great experience."

articles.title: Gladbach 2026/27 season preview: Transfers, pre-season, predicted lineup and predictions
articles.summary: Borussia Mönchengladbach are heading into the 2026/27 Bundesliga season with renewed optimism. After finishing 12th last season, the club decided to stick wi...
articles.body:
Borussia Mönchengladbach are heading into the 2026/27 Bundesliga season with renewed optimism. After finishing 12th last season, the club decided to stick with headcoach Eugen Polanski , despite some supporters calling for a change in the dugout.

The decision could prove to be a smart one. Gladbach have enjoyed an outstanding pre-season, strengthened their squad with an interesting group of young players and are set to welcome back one of their most important players in Tim Kleindienst .

There are still major questions to answer, particularly following the departure of former captain Rocco Reitz. But the Foals appear to have taken a step in the right direction.

If results are anything to go by, Gladbach have had one of the most impressive pre-seasons of any Bundesliga club.

The Foals won all eight of their pre-season matches , scoring an incredible 45 goals while conceding just seven .

Their summer campaign included comfortable victories over Wuppertal, Rot-Weiss Essen and Hansa Rostock before Gladbach produced arguably their most impressive result: a 4-1 win over Hoffenheim .

They also finished their friendly schedule with an eye-catching 2-1 victory over Aston Villa .

The results have naturally created plenty of optimism around the Borussia-Park. More importantly, Polanski appears to have developed a team that is comfortable both with the ball and in transition.

The momentum continued into competitive action.

Gladbach comfortably defeated Schott Mainz 5-0 in the first round of the DFB-Pokal, giving the club another confidence boost ahead of the Bundesliga campaign.

Perhaps the biggest boost of all, however, is the return of Tim Kleindienst .

The striker missed the entirety of last season, and his comeback has been highly anticipated in Gladbach. His physical presence, goalscoring ability and link-up play will give Polanski an entirely different attacking dimension.

There is also some continuity in goal. Gladbach decided to keep Moritz Nicolas despite interest in the goalkeeper, giving Polanski a reliable option between the posts.

The biggest question is whether the coach can translate this excellent pre-season form into a significant improvement in the Bundesliga.

Gladbach have taken an interesting approach to the summer transfer window.

Rather than relying exclusively on established Bundesliga names, the club have targeted talent from the 2. Bundesliga , looking to identify players capable of making the step up.

One of the headline arrivals is Isac Lidberg , who joined from Darmstadt. The Swedish striker scored 31 goals and provided nine assists in 58 2. Bundesliga appearances before making the move to Gladbach. He is expected to provide strong competition and cover for Kleindienst.

David Herold has also arrived from Karlsruhe, while Enzo Leopold joined from Hannover 96. Both players fit the club's strategy of recruiting relatively young players who still have room to develop.

There are also some particularly intriguing additions from abroad.

Ko Itakura has returned to Gladbach from Ajax, signing a contract until 2030. His return is especially significant because it directly addresses the departure of Nico Elvedi.

Young defenders Jan Leszczyński and Yukhym Konoplya have also joined, while Hugo Bolin has made his loan move permanent after impressing during his initial spell.

The departures, meanwhile, have been significant.

Most notably, former captain Rocco Reitz has joined RB Leipzig for around €20 million. Reitz leaves a sizeable hole in Gladbach's midfield - and there is an immediate twist to his departure: Leipzig host Gladbach on Matchday 1 , meaning Reitz will face his former club straight away.

Long-serving centre-back Nico Elvedi has also departed, joining Leeds United. After many years at Gladbach, the Swiss international had established himself as something of a modern-day club legend.

Then there is Giovanni Reyna . The American arrived from Borussia Dortmund with enormous expectations, but his time in Gladbach never really developed as hoped. He has now joined Strasbourg.

Polanski could opt for a 4-2-3-1 formation :

Predicted lineup (4-2-3-1): Nicolas – Hashioka, Diks, Itakura, Ullrich – Stöger, Sander – Mohya, Bolin, Hack – Kleindienst

The return of Kleindienst is the obvious headline. However, Lidberg provides an excellent alternative and could see plenty of minutes throughout the season.

Robin Hack is also expected to be an important figure after returning from injury. His availability adds another much-needed attacking option.

The youngster has already shown flashes of enormous potential and could emerge as Gladbach's next superstar . His performances last season suggested that there is plenty more to come, and the club will be hoping he can make the next step in 2026/27.

It is difficult not to be impressed by what Gladbach have done over the summer.

Eight wins from eight pre-season games, 45 goals scored and just seven conceded is an extraordinary record, even when taking the varying quality of opposition into account.

More importantly, the club appear to have invested intelligently.

The departure of Reitz is undoubtedly a major blow. He was not only an important midfielder but also the club captain, and replacing his influence will be one of Polanski's biggest challenges.

However, Gladbach have brought in several players who could collectively fill the void. Itakura adds experience, while Leopold, Herold, Lidberg and the other new arrivals give the squad additional depth and potential.

Kleindienst's return could be almost like a new signing. The striker has already demonstrated his quality at Bundesliga level and should once again put himself in the conversation for the German national team if he can return to his best form.

Compared with several of their direct Bundesliga rivals, Gladbach appear to have taken a step forward. The biggest question mark for this writer is therefore not necessarily the squad - it is Polanski .

The club have placed their trust in the former midfielder after last season's 12th-place finish. Now, he has to demonstrate that he can take this group to the next level.

The Foals should have enough quality to stay comfortably away from the relegation battle, while their attacking options and Kleindienst's return could allow them to challenge for the upper half of the table.

A push for Europe might be a little too ambitious at this stage, but a strong campaign could lay the foundations for one in the future.

Gladbach may not be ready to return to their best just yet, but the signs point towards a much more stable and promising season - and if Polanski can get the most out of his talented squad, the Foals could surprise a few people.

articles.title: After slow start, Steele rolls past Reagan 52-21 in football season opener
articles.summary: The Knights fell behind twice in the first half but scored 45 straight points to put away the Rattlers in a season-opening matchup between 6A heavyweights.
articles.body:
Steele players had just taken the field before they raced right back to the locker room when lightning delayed their highly anticipated season opener.

When play finally began about 90 minutes later, it took a while for the Knights to get going. And when they did, it resulted in a 52-21 victory against Reagan on Thursday night at Comalander Stadium.

"It was the first game of the season, of course, we were all excited and hyped up running out of the tunnel," Steele's Ohio State bound senior free safety Eli Johnson said. "We hear the band going crazy, and then it gets delayed. So, we had to face a little adversity, and we just had to learn how to build off that."

The third-ranked Knights battled from behind twice before rolling to their sixth straight victory in a season opener. Steele outgained No. 7 Reagan 434-112 in total yardage. Most of the Rattlers' offense was generated in the first half.

Senior quarterback DJ Green passed for 205 yards with scores of 91 and 30 yards. He also rushed four times for 52 yards and a touchdown. Junior running back Liam Jones had 154 yards and two touchdowns on 14 carries.

"I love making plays with my teammates," Green said. "It definitely starts with the o-line, and then everybody else comes between it. Making plays is my thing."

It certainly didn't start that way after the Knights opened with a three-and-out. Reagan responded with a six-play, 48-yard drive capped by Jeriko Espinoza's 26-yard scoring catch from Jace Huesser for a 7-0 lead.

After another three-and-out, the Knights finally got it going when Jones raced in from 57 yards on the first play of their third drive to tie it at 7 with 4:00 left in the first quarter.

Reagan summoned two of its top defenders to take a 14-7 lead early in the second quarter. Linebacker Ayden Fernandez recovered a Steele muff on the Knights' 27. Two plays later, he lined up at wildcat and rushed three times for 21 yards. Defensive back Ricky Armstong then lined up at wildcat and scored from four yards.

Well, that was about it for the Rattlers.

Steele scored on its next four possessions to close the half for a 31-14 lead. Green got the run started with a 16-yard scoring run. Fortune then fell the Knights way when left tackle Alexander Fisher recovered a fumble in the end zone for a 21-14 lead at the 5:51 mark.

Johnson set up the next two scores with big punt returns. His 30-yard return led to Ralph Lara's 34-yard field goal. The Knights turned Johnson's 19-yard return to a 7-yard scoring run by Jones.

"We have an abundance of leaders," Johnson said. "Everyone had their heads up, stayed positive and just knew if we stayed positive, momentum would come back our way."

The Knights carried that momentum over to the second half with three touchdowns and a 52-14 lead. Green connected with Jamin Harwell for a 91-yard catch-and-run and with Jayden Casiano for a 30-yard score on fourth-and-11. They sandwiched those scores around Kemarrion Smith's 1-yard TD run set up by Green's 45-yard pass to Tanner Mudge.

"We got together as a team," Green said. "We don't really beat each other up. We just stayed together the whole time."

The Knights, ranked No. 20 in the state, next face two heavy-hitters before beginning District 27-6A play as they travel for a road game at No. 11 Humble Atascocita next week before hosting No. 19 Lake Travis in two weeks.

"This is a great feeling," Green said. "There's definitely some mistakes that need to be fixed, but it's good to know that the hard work we are putting in is working."

articles.title: Bayern Munich season preview: What is the aim for Kompany, Kane and Bundesliga champions?
articles.summary: Bayern Munich start their latest title defence as overwhelming odds-on favourites to win the Bundesliga again - so what would constitute success?
articles.body:
Bayern Munich start their latest title defence as overwhelming odds-on favourites to win the Bundesliga again - so what would consistute success this season?

The German side are as short as 1-7 odds with bookmakers after winning 13 of the past 14 titles - and are chasing a hat-trick of successes.

They host Stuttgart on Friday (19:30 BST) in a game you can watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website.

Vincent Kompany's side already have a win against rivals Borussia Dortmund under their belt after winning the German Super Cup 2-1 last weekend.

England captain Harry Kane will be looking to win his fourth Bundesliga Golden Boot in four seasons... and perhaps even more.

"The targets at Bayern are always set as high as possible, which means winning the Bundesliga, winning the cup, winning the Champions League and perhaps even winning every single match," said Kompany this summer.

BBC Sport has a look at what Bayern and Kane can hope for this season - and what is new.

Watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app.

Kane first Englishman to win Germany's player of the year award

Winning the Bundesliga title is more of an expectation than a cause for huge celebration at the Allianz Arena.

Since 2012 only once have they not been champions - when Bayer Leverkusen went unbeaten all season domestically in 2023-24.

In Kompany's two seasons at Bayern, since leaving Burnley, they have finished 13 and 16 points clear at the top.

Last season the German double winners were one of Europe's biggest entertainers, scoring 184 goals in all competitions.

They scored a record 122 goals in the Bundesliga and 43 in the Champions League, where they fell to Paris St-Germain 6-5 on aggregate in the semi-finals.

Since this era of dominance started with the 2012-13 Treble, including the Champions League, they have only won Europe's top trophy once since then - in 2020.

But German football writer Constantin Eckner says Kompany does "not necessarily" need to win it this season.

"Bayern's hierarchy have been very happy with him and the progress of the team," said Eckner.

"As long as they compete among the top four in Europe, they are content to have Kompany. He has brought back a notion of stability to Bayern's managerial post.

"Before that, it was quite the revolving door policy, as they had seven managers in eight years.

"The Belgian has been a revelation, and the feeling is he could become one of the best managers in the world.

"One could argue he is already among the best, though games like the one at Paris St-Germain have shown that he still has a few things to learn."

When Kane joined Bayern on a four-year deal in 2022 from Tottenham there was a feeling, certainly in England, that he might return home at the end of that deal.

Kane had never won a trophy during his time at Tottenham, or with England, so the pull of going to a team who win trophies nearly every year was strong.

But many also thought after bagging a few medals he would perhaps try to break the Premier League goalscoring record (sitting 47 behind Alan Shearer).

In fact he admitted as much last week, saying: "When I first left, for sure it was something I thought - I would definitely be coming back. That itch isn't there as much anymore."

The 33-year-old has loved his time at Bayern and says he is ready to begin discussions over extending that deal.

That love is very much mutual. Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness has called Kane "the best signing we've ever made".

This is a club who have had some legendary goalscorers in Gerd Muller, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge and Robert Lewandowski.

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign.

That took his total to 146 goals - plus 33 assists - in 147 games for Bayern. He won the European Shoe in 2024 and 2026 and 'just' the regular Bundesliga Golden Boot in 2025.

He also scored all three goals in the German Cup final win over Stuttgart to complete the 2026 double.

"There are many fans who believe he could win the Ballon d'Or," said Eckner.

"Bayern are lobbying for it [and it is] also a sign towards the much younger Michael Olise that a move to Real Madrid wouldn't be necessary to win the Ballon d'Or.

"Kane has impressed with his very consistent and relentless goalscoring in the Bundesliga. He has essentially filled the shoes of Robert Lewandowksi, who put up similar numbers.

"Bayern rely heavily on Kane. They haven't signed a real back-up for him, nor a potential replacement. His contract runs out at the end of the season, but Bayern are sure he will extend for a few more years."

Were Kane to win the Ballon d'Or he would be only the second Englishman to win it since the 1970s and the first since Michael Owen in 2001.

"The Ballon d'Or is as big as it gets, from an individual point of view," he said.

"It's not in my hands. I've done what I can do in terms of putting in the performances. It's now down to votes and other people and the media - stuff I can't control - so we'll see what happens."

However last November Kane admitted: "I could score 100 goals this season, but if I don't win the Champions League or the World Cup, you're probably not going to win the Ballon d'Or."

He lost in the semi-final of both competitions.

Another one of Bayern's irreplaceable players is another Londoner in Olise, who represents France at international level.

The forward has scored 43 goals - including one in this season's Super Cup - with 46 assists in just over two years at the club.

Bayern have made little changes rather than a squad overhaul this summer, not surprising after two good seasons.

They have recruited Germany left-back Nathaniel Brown from Eintracht Frankfurt for a fee thought to be about £47m.

The 23-year-old can also play on the wing - and even featured in the number 10 role in the Super Cup, where he scored on his debut.

The other big signing is Morocco international Ismael Saibari from PSV for a reported £43m.

Like Brown, the 27-year-old is versatile and can play in midfield or anywhere up front. He scored three times at the World Cup.

The highest profile exits have been Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka, 31, and versatile Portuguese wideman Raphael Guerreiro, 32.

Both have left as free agents at the end of their contracts.

Senegal striker Nicolas Jackson returned to Chelsea at the end of his season-long loan.

Bayern will also have to manage the situation with Jamal Musiala this season.

The 23-year-old attacking midfielder says he is being treated for a "neurological dysfunction" after collapsing during two friendlies this summer.

He added they were "temporary, brief, but easily treatable absence seizures".

"I'm receiving excellent medical treatment and am very optimistic," he continued.

"FC Bayern and my family and friends are always by my side and supporting me on this journey."
